messages.content: My wife and I have nine days available in late September, but we only want seven nights away. We are comparing the St. Simons/Jekyll area with Tybee Island and Savannah. Can you help us choose both the dates and whether it makes more sense to drive from Atlanta or fly and rent a car?
Yes. What are the first and last dates in the nine-day period, and should I compare costs for both of you together? I will also need to know whether you expect to use a car throughout the trip.

We are free from Saturday, September 20 through Sunday, September 28. Compare the total for two adults. We would share one hotel room. In either area we would want a car for beach access, meals, and day trips.

That gives you two straightforward seven-night spans: Saturday September 20 to Saturday September 27, or Sunday September 21 to Sunday September 28. I can compare Atlanta driving costs with airfare for two plus an eight-day rental. Should I use a standard midsize car and include parking, fuel, and likely airport charges?

Yes. Also account for the fact that we would need to get from Atlanta airport back home after returning the rental. We can use about $45 each way for that. We would leave our own car at home if we fly.

Understood. For Tybee/Savannah, the drive is about 250 miles each way and generally 4 to 4.5 hours without a long stop. For St. Simons or Jekyll, it is roughly 310 to 325 miles each way and about 5 to 5.5 hours. I’ll compare those with flights from Atlanta to Savannah and Brunswick, including a rental car and the $90 home-airport transfer total.
Please do. We are not trying to avoid driving at all costs. I mainly want to know whether flying actually saves enough time to justify the added expense.

For September 20-27, current sample totals for two are approximately: drive to Tybee/Savannah, $245 including fuel, estimated wear allowance, and hotel parking; fly to Savannah and rent a car, $1,040 including two round trips, rental, taxes, fuel, airport transfers, and hotel parking. Door to door, flying saves only about 1 to 1.5 hours each way after airport time. For St. Simons/Jekyll, driving is about $315. Flying to Brunswick with a rental is near $1,180 and has limited schedules; flying to Savannah and driving south is about $1,025 but takes nearly as long door to door as driving from Atlanta.
That makes driving look fairly clear. Are the Sunday-to-Sunday figures materially different?

The driving totals change very little. For September 21-28, Tybee/Savannah remains about $245, while St. Simons/Jekyll is about $315. The sample airfare is lower on the Sunday departure: Savannah flights plus the rental total about $910 for Tybee and about $925 if you continue to the Golden Isles. Brunswick is still the costliest option at roughly $1,110. Even with the lower fares, flying adds about $600 to $865 over driving.
How much vacation time do we lose by driving to each? We could leave Atlanta around 8:30 in the morning on either start date.

Leaving at 8:30 a.m., you would likely reach Savannah around 1:00 p.m. and Tybee around 1:30, allowing for one stop. St. Simons would be around 2:00 p.m., and Jekyll around 2:15. Those arrivals line up reasonably well with afternoon hotel check-in. A flight might put you on Tybee around noon if every step goes smoothly, but the Brunswick-area options would generally place you there between 1:00 and 3:00 p.m. because of schedules and rental pickup.

Then remove flying to Brunswick. Keep the Savannah flight only as a benchmark, not as the likely choice. Now compare the two date spans from a destination standpoint. I am concerned about weekend crowds and hotel prices.

September 20-27 places your first night on Saturday but has a Saturday checkout. September 21-28 avoids paying for the opening Saturday night, though it includes the following Saturday night and a Sunday return. Preliminary one-room lodging samples show the Sunday-to-Sunday span about $110 lower around St. Simons/Jekyll and about $70 lower around Tybee/Savannah. Tybee’s weekends show the sharper rate increase and more two-night restrictions. The Golden Isles sample is steadier across both spans.
What about the practical difference between the areas? We want beach time, but seven nights is long enough that we need more than sitting on the sand.

Tybee/Savannah offers the broader non-beach mix: Savannah’s historic district, museums, architecture, restaurants, and riverfront are about 25 to 40 minutes from Tybee depending on traffic. The tradeoff is heavier weekend traffic, paid parking, and a busier beach setting. St. Simons/Jekyll offers quieter coastal days, bike routes, maritime and historic sites, nature centers, and easy movement between the islands. Brunswick adds dining and a small historic core, but the overall sightseeing range is narrower than Savannah’s.
Could we stay in Savannah and drive to Tybee, or does that defeat the beach part of the trip?

It is workable, but it changes the trip. Staying in Savannah can reduce some hotel rates and makes evenings in the city easier, while each beach day requires a 35- to 50-minute drive each way in typical traffic plus Tybee parking fees. A split stay could preserve both experiences, but changing hotels during a seven-night trip adds packing and check-in time. For lodging research, it would be useful to compare Tybee beachfront or walk-to-beach rooms against Savannah hotels with included or reasonably priced parking.
Do not split the stay yet. Which combinations are strongest if we care about overall value, useful things to do, and not spending a large part of the first and last day in transit?

The strongest overall-value combination is St. Simons/Jekyll, Sunday September 21 to Sunday September 28, driving from Atlanta. It has the lowest sampled lodging week for that area, predictable transportation costs, and arrival near check-in time. The strongest activity-rich combination is Tybee/Savannah on the same Sunday-to-Sunday dates, also driving. It costs somewhat more and has more weekend congestion, but provides the widest range of non-beach options. Saturday September 20-27 in either area is a useful backup if Sunday travel becomes inconvenient, though the sample lodging totals are higher.
Can you put approximate trip totals on those two leading combinations before we move to specific hotels? Include transportation and a realistic lodging allowance, but leave meals and activities out.

Using current sample lodging rather than bookable selections: St. Simons/Jekyll, September 21-28, driving, is about $2,205 total: $1,890 for seven nights including estimated lodging taxes and $315 for driving, fuel, and parking. Tybee/Savannah, September 21-28, driving, is about $2,515 total: $2,270 for seven nights including estimated taxes and $245 for transportation and parking. The Savannah-flight benchmark for the Tybee option would raise that total to about $3,180. Rates can change, and no room, flight, or car has been held.

Keep both Sunday-to-Sunday driving options for hotel research. Make St. Simons/Jekyll the value leader and Tybee/Savannah the broader-activities alternative. Retain Saturday-to-Saturday only as a date fallback. Nothing should be booked yet.

Shortlist for the next lodging search: leader, drive from Atlanta for seven nights September 21-28 in the St. Simons/Jekyll area, with a preliminary transportation-plus-lodging total of about $2,205. Alternative, drive for the same dates and stay in the Tybee/Savannah area, about $2,515, offering the broader selection of city activities. September 20-27 remains a fallback span for either destination. Flying through Savannah is only a cost and timing benchmark; Brunswick flights are removed. Nothing has been booked or held, and the next step is to compare one-room hotel options within each leading area.
